paragraphs: Friend, this passage is about what a covenant friend looks like when it costs something. Jonathan makes a covenant with David, and then he keeps it with his father's spear flying at him. Saul even tells Jonathan that as long as David lives, “neither you nor your kingdom shall be established” (1 Samuel 20:31). Jonathan still says, “Whatever you desire, I will do for you” (1 Samuel 20:4).

Look at what Jonathan's love does. It stands up to Saul when he asks, “Why must he be put to death? What has he done?” (1 Samuel 20:32). And it keeps showing up after the worst day of the whole story, because Jonathan was grieved by his father's shameful treatment of David (1 Samuel 20:34), and I think that grief is why he went out to that field the next morning. Real loyalty keeps its word even when it hurts.

So here's your question, baker: who is in your corner when things get scary, and who are you in the corner for? Be that friend, even when it's costly. When David and Jonathan weep and part, they say, “May the LORD be a witness between you and me” (1 Samuel 20:42). They didn't hold up their friendship alone, and neither do you, and this story isn't over, so keep your oven warm.
